# Tin density

> Every published tin density disagrees. This page gathers 75 records from 39 source documents,
> each with the verbatim line it was read from and a link to that page.

## Answers

- White tin (beta) at 20 C: 7.287 g/cm3 (18 records, 17 sources; range 7.265 to 7.336)
- Grey tin (alpha) at 20 C: 5.769 g/cm3 (8 records, 8 sources)
- Liquid tin at melting: 6.983 g/cm3 (6 sources; primary measurement 0.05 percent)
- Sn63Pb37 solder: 8.40 g/cm3 (8 sources, range 8.340 to 8.420)
- SAC305 solder: 7.40 g/cm3 (6 sources; two give 7.49 and 7.50, mixtures predict 7.361)
- Sn100C: 7.40 g/cm3 (3 sources)
- Sn96.5Ag3.5: 7.36 g/cm3 (one maker)
- Pewter and white metal: 7.28 g/cm3 (one ASM table each)
- Tin babbitt grades 1 to S: 7.34 to 7.75 g/cm3
- Tin powder, apparent: 3.2 to 3.8 g/cm3 (not the metal density)

## Data

- [Spreadsheet](https://engreaved.github.io/tin-density/DATA/tin-density.xlsx): three sheets, all records with URL and verbatim quote
- [CSV](https://engreaved.github.io/tin-density/DATA/tin-density.csv): the same rows as text
- [Full page](https://engreaved.github.io/tin-density/): every record with its quote and link

## Notes

- Values are nominal, not certified reference material.
- Only 15 of 75 records state a temperature.
- Gamma and delta high-pressure phases are computed only and are not pooled with measurements.
- Six of eight categories fall short of ten independent sources, and the shortfall is stated rather than filled.
- Source values remain their publishers' property; this compilation adds the selection and the exclusion record.
